overview:
Goal: make Lucid as fast as possible on mid- and low-end Android phones (mobile profile: 1.6 Mbps, 150 ms RTT, CPU 4x), without weakening offline support, a11y, the CSP, privacy or any tested behaviour.

The four diagnoses agree on where the time goes:
- **Cold loads** are network-bound. Four causes:
  - Today, real-life and scenarios download 214 KB gz of JSON and use about 1% of it.
  - Reading, listening, speaking, **drills and level checks** download all 75 lessons (cold checkpoint/A1: 7320 ms, 107 requests, 1065 KB gz; re-measured in this review).
  - Module and content requests are discovered late, one round trip at a time.
- **Returning visits** are slow only because code is network-first in the service worker. A return after 10 minutes takes 1.3 s, after any push to main 2.1 s, on lie-fi 16 s.
- **Releases** download all 884 KB again and delete the lessons the learner saved for offline use.
- **CPU**: it matters only for learners with history (heavy warm Today 1066 ms at 4x), plus a few first-use Intl and recompute long tasks, plus per-row Intl construction in the vocab list.

Interactions (lesson Check 40 ms, essay typing 8 ms median per key) are already fine. They are guarded as non-regression targets, not optimised.

**Plan: four lanes in separate worktrees, no hand-edited file owned by two lanes.**
- **runtime**: the measurement harness, plus the learner model, store and vocab CPU work.
- **content**: generated indexes, split content and per-level pool files, and every view and module that consumes them.
- **boot**: index.html, app.js, router, preload hints, route-graph and data prefetch, the page side of release updates, perceived-load and CLS fixes.
- **delivery**: the service worker, the manifest and release hashing, the deploy-time minify step, CI verification and docs.

**Merge order**
1. runtime R1 (the harness) together with R9 (adaptive reads index rows), which the other lanes' acceptance checks need.
2. content C1 and delivery D1: the generator and the hashes.
3. Everything else, in priority order within each lane. Generated files (content/manifest.json, release.json, the RELEASE line of sw.js, js/core/route-deps.js) are never hand-merged: a conflict is resolved by re-running their generator (contract C-12).

**What stays and what is gated**
- The source stays buildless (ADR-1). Every new artefact is either a static JSON or JS file generated by a tools/ script and committed, or a deploy-only transform.
- The deploy-time esbuild minify step is planned. It is kept only if, on the integrated tree, it still cuts at least 200 ms from cold welcome and from cold Today. It keeps every path, publishes source maps, pins esbuild exactly, recomputes the release hashes on the built bytes, and falls back to deploying the unminified source on any error, so the other sites in pages.yml are never blocked.
- Inlining the CSS is a separate item, gated on its own measurement.

**Expected integrated result on the phone, mostly already measured on prototypes**
- Cold welcome 2050 → about 1400 ms, with first paint at about 0.6 s.
- Cold Today 3695 → about 1900 ms, 426 → about 170 KB gz.
- Cold reading 7172 → about 2300 ms; cold level check 7320 → about 2300 ms.
- Return after 10 minutes or after a deploy: 1.3 to 2.1 s → about 0.4 s.
- Heavy-history warm Today 1066 → about 700 ms.
- Desktop CLS 0.5 → 0.

**How to measure**
Every acceptance number comes from `node tools/perf.mjs` with 3 or more runs, median, compared against the lane's own base commit on the same machine, or from a unit or e2e test. The lead re-runs the full suite on the merged result and writes docs/perf/after.md.

**Review verification (scratch copies under scratchpad/perf/check, mobile profile, 3 runs, median, two runs in parallel so only relative numbers count)**
- D2 cache-first code (proto1 sw.js) vs base, returning learner: stale Today 1284 → 417 ms, stale lesson 1234 → 367; after a push Today 2111 → 435, lesson 1810 → 351; fresh Today 428 → 435 (no regression). Confirmed.
- C2 index files (content-data proto) vs base: cold Today 3679 → 2462 ms, 426 → 226 KB gz, welcome unchanged (2065 vs 2069). Confirmed, within the plan's standalone target. The same prototype's precache grew from 84 requests / 884 KB to 152 / 1094 KB (centre files and per-item files listed), which D4 must undo.
- New: cold #/checkpoint/A1 on base: 7320 ms, 107 requests, 1065 KB gz; first-session Today → checkpoint 6286 ms; returning 391 ms. Drills use the same pool (pool.js exercisePool → content.allLessons).
- New: Node micro-benchmark, 700 vocab words: `new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` per row 35.4 ms vs 0.4 ms with one shared object; sort with `localeCompare(b, 'en', {sensitivity})` 29.4 ms vs 0.4 ms with one Intl.Collator (unthrottled; roughly 4x on the phone).

Review changes:
1. Added C10 (P0): per-level pool files for drills and level checks. The plan had rejected this as 'not measured'; re-measured here at 7.3 s cold and 6.3 s first-session transition, the same class of problem as reading. pool.js moves into the content lane; B3, R1, C-1, C-2 and targets updated.
2. Added R9 (P0) and contract C-11: adaptive.writingMinutes reads task.items?.length, but the writing index rows carry n_items (checked in the prototype index), so C2 alone would change Today's plan minutes for sentence-exercise tasks. adaptive.js is runtime-owned, so the fix is a runtime item merged with R1.
3. Rewrote R8: the heavy vocab cost is mainly a new RelativeTimeFormat per row (vocab.js:31, called per row at :102) and a collator built per comparison in the sort (:74). The old content-visibility R8 is moved to rejected. This also removes runtime's share of css/app.css, which is now boot-only.
4. Rewrote R6: removed 'first render with toLowerCase ordering, re-sort after idle'. Reordering a rendered list shifts layout and moves rows under a screen reader. It now uses shared module-level Intl objects plus an idle warm-up; the order is identical from the first frame.
5. D1: the release hash now includes sw.js, with its RELEASE line normalised. Otherwise a release that changes only sw.js (scenario u) keeps the same RELEASE and cache name. The per-file hashes move to a separate release.json that only the worker and tools read. Lesson hashes are added so carried-over saved lessons can be checked. manifest.json, which B1 makes boot-critical, keeps its current shape and size. C-5 updated.
6. D4: corrected the risk. cache:'no-cache' always revalidates, so the browser HTTP cache cannot store a stale copy. The real risk is a CDN edge serving the previous deploy, which D5's hash check covers. Also added a request-count target, because per-item split files add about 70 precache requests.
7. D5: a hash mismatch is retried once with a cache-busting query. If it still mismatches, the install fails, so the old release stays. Saved lessons are carried over only if their hash is unchanged.
8. B6 and contract C-4 rewritten:
   - The reload happens inside router.go, after the old view's cleanup and a store flush, and only for path changes (never query-only changes). The old route blacklist could skip cleanup-time saves.
   - Every tab, including one that did not trigger the activation, reloads at its next path change instead of importing a new-release module.
   - The hidden-tab trigger is limited to non-bare routes.
   - Added registration.update() when the tab becomes visible after more than 1 hour, because an SPA rarely navigates. With cache-first code, a learner who resumes the app from the background would otherwise not get updates.
9. C4: centre files are not precached. Offline, a learner who never opened Reading online would get an error where today they see the exercises from their saved lessons. Added a fallback to the cached-lessons path. C10 uses the same fallback.
10. B5 wording: the module script is at the end of <body> today. B5 (proto3b) moves it into the head, before the in-body stylesheet. The rejected 'moving the module script to the end of <body>' is reworded: it was proto3, keeping the script after the in-body stylesheet.
11. D7: the fallback also runs `git clean -fdq -- .` inside lucid/, so a half-finished build cannot ship stray .map files.
12. Ownership fixes:
    - css/app.css is now boot-only.
    - New lane e2e files tests/e2e/perf-boot.mjs (boot) and tests/e2e/perf-runtime.mjs (runtime), because the content lane owns the existing e2e files. B4, B6 and R6 had needed e2e edits in files they did not own.
    - js/core/pool.js and a new tests/unit/pool.test.mjs go to content.
    - Merge rule for generated files (C-12).
13. Rejected list:
    - Removed 'per-level pool files' (now C10).
    - Reworded 'caching Intl objects' (it holds only for first-use cost).
    - Added 'content-visibility on vocab rows' and 'deferred collation re-sort'.
targets: Mobile, cold first visit #/welcome (scenario a): view ≤ 1450 ms (baseline 2050); first paint and FCP ≤ 700 ms (baseline 2072); CLS 0; TBT ≤ 50 ms.
Mobile, cold #/today, onboarded A1 learner (scenario b): view ≤ 1950 ms (baseline 3695; index alone re-measured 2462); FCP ≤ 700 ms; ≤ 180 KB gz on the wire (baseline 426); TBT ≤ 60 ms.

Mobile, other cold routes (scenario c): lesson/a1-01 ≤ 2100 ms (3159), real-life ≤ 1850 (3527), scenario ≤ 1900 (3563), writing ≤ 2050 (2766), writing/final-B2 ≤ 2600 (3739), games ≤ 1850 (2885), expressions ≤ 2200 (3495), reading ≤ 2400 (7172) with ≤ 35 requests, progress ≤ 1750 (2610), checkpoint/A1 ≤ 2300 (7320, re-measured) with ≤ 30 requests and ≤ 300 KB gz (1065), drill?topic=<A1 topic> ≤ 2300 with ≤ 30 requests.

Mobile, warm repeat visit to #/today with the service worker active, by HTTP-cache state: fresh ≤ 390 ms (no regression from 378-428); stale, more than 10 min later (--http-maxage 0), ≤ 450 ms (1269-1284; prototype 417); after a push to main changes every ETag ≤ 450 ms (2099-2111; prototype 435); offline ≤ 420 ms (398); lie-fi ≤ 500 ms (16471). Lesson a1-01 ≤ 400 ms in each state (baseline 1234-1243 stale, 1726-1810 after a push, 24412 lie-fi).

Mobile, returning learner after a new release: Today ≤ 420 ms (1115). The release update downloads only changed files plus ≤ 5 KB (baseline 884 KB). Saved offline lessons whose content did not change are kept 100% (baseline 0%).

Mobile, first-session route transitions from Today while the worker installs (scenario d): lesson ≤ 800 ms (1911); reading ≤ 300 ms (4157); checkpoint/A1 ≤ 700 ms (6286); writing ≤ 350 ms (297; must not regress to the measured 1112); games ≤ 550 ms (409 baseline; no regression); real-life ≤ 300 ms (453).
Mobile, returning route transitions: every route ≤ 120 ms except reading ≤ 100 ms (382) and checkpoint/A1 ≤ 150 ms (391); progress and writing with 0 long tasks.
Mobile, first-visit service-worker precache (scenario f): ≤ 700 KB on the wire (884; the unmodified index prototype measured 1094) and ≤ 160 requests, finished ≤ 8.5 s after welcome (9.45 s).

Heavy-history learner (180 days, 5.3k attempts, about 700 cards), warm, CPU 4x: Today ≤ 750 ms (1066); TBT ≤ 160 ms (377); longest task ≤ 120 ms (247). Review → back to Today ≤ 160 ms (319-360). Today → progress ≤ 130 ms (194-224). Today → reading TBT ≤ 10 ms (94). Today → vocab ≤ 100 ms (169), longest task ≤ 60 ms.
Lesson Check → verdict (choice) ≤ 45 ms and INP ≤ 48 (baseline 40/40). Last match pair ≤ 75 ms (71). Word-quiz round start with no long task over 50 ms (baseline 85-98 ms task).
Essay typing, 300 words: per-key median ≤ 10 ms, p95 ≤ 22 ms, INP ≤ 30 ms, 0 slow events (baseline 8/20/24/0).
Desktop: CLS ≤ 0.01 on every cold and warm load (baseline 0.186-0.500). View times stay within +15 ms of baseline.

Release freshness: after a deploy, a returning learner runs the new release's code no later than the first path change (or reload) after the new worker finishes installing; 0 page loads mix modules from two releases, including with two tabs open.

Guardrails on every lane merge:
- npm test (all unit tests), the full e2e suite (including axe a11y and the offline check) and npm run validate pass.
- No console errors on the 13-route sweep plus checkpoint and drill.
- The CSP meta is byte-identical.
- No new origins in connect-src.

lanes.title: Measurement harness, learner-model, store and vocab CPU

items.title: Harness: heavy learner, returning-visit states, release-update scenario, drill and checkpoint routes, cheaper visibility probe
items.fix:
Add to tools/perf.mjs; existing flags keep their meaning:
- --learner light|heavy. heavy is a deterministic seed built through the app's own modules: pinned PRNG, history relative to today, 180 days, 32 lessons, about 5k attempts, 1.2k events, 700 cards.
- --http-maxage N.
- --etag-epoch: rotate ETag and Last-Modified on every file to model a push to main.
- --net offline|lie-fi: lie-fi holds every response for 15 s.
- Scenario g: returning Today and lesson in the states fresh, stale, after-push, offline and lie-fi. Port extra.mjs scenario r from the perceived-offline prototype.
- Scenario u: a release that changes only sw.js. Record the bytes it downloads, cached lessons before and after, Today → lesson while the new worker installs, and which release each loaded module came from (for B6).
- Add VIEW selectors 'checkpoint/' → '[data-begin]' and 'drill' → the drill's first exercise. Add checkpoint/A1 and drill?topic=<an A1 topic> to the default route list for scenarios c and d.
- Heavy transitions back to Today in scenario d, and Today → vocab.
- Restrict the visible() probe to requestAnimationFrame only, or an IntersectionObserver.
Record the learner and the state in the JSON.
items.acceptance:
- Re-running light scenarios a-f on the unchanged base reproduces docs/perf/baseline.json within ±5% on every view median.
- Heavy warm Today at 4x reproduces 1066 ms within ±10%.
- Scenario g on the base gives stale Today 1269 ms ±10% and after-push 2099 ms ±10%.
- Cold checkpoint/A1 on the base gives 7320 ms ±10%.
- Probe overhead is ≤ 5 ms of forced layout per transition (CPU profile).
- Merged before other lanes record final numbers.
items.risk: Longer runs: the heavy seed takes about 3 s unthrottled per run. A seed that drifts with the date makes numbers unstable, so pin the PRNG and keep history relative to today. Changing the probe can shift every number, which is why the baseline must be reproduced first. Harness only, so no user-facing risk.

items.title: adaptive.writingMinutes and the plan accept writing-index rows (contract C-11)
items.problem: adaptive.js:305 computes a sentence task's minutes from task.items?.length. The writing index rows (C1) carry n_items instead of items, as checked in the content prototype's index. With C2 alone, writingMinutes returns null for sentence-exercise tasks, and Today's plan minutes change.
items.fix: In adaptive.writingMinutes, use `const n = task.n_items ?? task.items?.length` in place of task.items?.length. Audit learner.js and adaptive.js for any other read of items, practice or full-item fields on scenario or writing objects; today the grep finds only writingMinutes, plus id, level, stage, module, word_range, min_words, max_words, title_en and title_he, all of which stay in the index rows.
items.acceptance:
- writing-minutes.test: for every writing exercise and assignment, writingMinutes(indexRow) === writingMinutes(fullTask), using rows built the way C1 builds them.
- All unit tests pass.
- Merged together with R1, before C2.
items.risk: None: full tasks behave as before, because n_items is absent on them.

items.title: skillLevels sorts the attempts once; ISO timestamps compared with '<'
items.problem: model() → skillLevels runs firstTries(byTime(attempts)) inside the per-skill loop and again for checks (adaptive.js:154-195, confirmed). That is about 9 sorts of 5.3k attempts. adaptive.js:368 uses localeCompare on ISO strings, which pays about 21 ms of ICU collator start-up. model() costs 182 ms per heavy Today load.
items.fix: Compute `sorted = byTime(attempts)` and `first = firstTries(sorted)` once before the loop. Derive the checks from sorted.filter(a => a.source === 'checkpoint'). Replace localeCompare at :368 with plain < and > on the ISO strings; equal values keep their order, as the sort is stable. Patch reference: scratchpad js-runtime/opt5.patch.
items.acceptance:
- Heavy warm Today at 4x ≤ 900 ms (base 1066) and TBT ≤ 200 ms (377).
- Heavy review → Today ≤ 170 ms (319-360).
- model-equivalence.test: model() output deep-equals the pre-change output on the heavy seed and on the light seed.
- All unit tests pass.
items.risk: None by construction: same sort and same firstTries. The equivalence test guards it.

items.title: util.dayOf(iso) and string day comparisons in learner.js
items.problem: Every isToday and created_at day check builds a Date and calls toISOString per record (learner.js:273, 390, 402, 441, 484, 503, 526). todayKey self time is 61-90 ms on a heavy Today. todayKey is the UTC day (util.js:63), so slicing a canonical ISO string gives the same key.
items.fix: In util.js, export dayOf(iso): it returns iso.slice(0,10) for a 24-character string ending in 'Z' and falls back to todayKey(new Date(iso)) otherwise. Also export the helpers that contract C-3 lists. Use dayOf at every learner.js site. Make weekActivity compare a.at against start.toISOString() as strings, with the same canonical guard.
items.acceptance:
- todayKey and dayOf self time ≤ 5 ms in a heavy Today CPU profile (base 61-90).
- With R2: heavy warm Today ≤ 850 ms.
- Unit test: dayOf equals todayKey(new Date(x)) for 10,000 random canonical ISO strings, and for non-canonical strings (offsets, no ms, Date objects).
items.risk: Synced timestamps that are not in '…Z' form take the old path, so results are identical.

items.title: openStore reads IndexedDB once
items.problem: openStore calls idb.load() as a probe and throws the rows away (store.js:219). store.load() then calls getAll again (:226 → :87). Each read costs 125-140 ms for a 7.3k-record learner at 4x.
items.fix: Change store.load to load(preloaded = null), using preloaded || await backend.load(). openStore keeps the probe's rows and passes them in. The probe still decides between IndexedDB and memory.
items.acceptance:
- Unit test: exactly 1 backend.load per openStore, using a counting backend.
- Heavy warm Today ≥ 80 ms faster than R2+R3 at 4x (measured −100).
- store-sync and eraseDevice tests pass.
items.risk: Minimal: same rows, same order, same fallback when IndexedDB throws.

items.title: Memoise word senses in wordgame round building
items.problem: makeRound → distractors → shareSense (wordgame.js:74) calls senses() for both words on every comparison. senses() does a regex split plus an NFKC normalize, which makes an 85-98 ms long task at every round start.
items.fix: Add a module-level `senseMemo = new Map()` keyed by the Hebrew string; shareSense uses the memo. Optionally also memoise normalize(w[field]) inside distractors.
items.acceptance:
- Today → #/games/A1/1 has 0 long tasks over 50 ms (base 85-98 ms).
- The transition is ≥ 40 ms faster for the light learner at 4x (base 259).
- wordgame.test passes, and seeded rounds are identical before and after.
items.risk: None: senses() is pure, and the memo holds at most a few thousand entries. Callers must not mutate the returned Set; none do today.

items.title: Remove the first-use Intl cost from hot first renders, with the same output from the first frame
items.problem: The first use of each Intl formatter costs 18-39 ms at 4x CPU. progress.js:29 (weekday labels via toLocaleDateString) is the only long task on Today → progress. vocab.js and slang.js pay for RelativeTimeFormat and the collator on first open.
items.fix:
- progress.js: static narrow-weekday tables (he: א׳…ש׳, en: S M T W T F S) indexed by getDay().
- util.js: export groupDigits(n) for consumers in the content lane.
- util.js: export collatorEn() and relTime(lang), memoised module-level Intl objects. Also export warmIntl(), which builds both in requestIdleCallback. Boot calls warmIntl once after the first route renders (contract C-3), so the first open of vocab or expressions finds them ready.
- vocab.js and slang.js use these shared objects.
The list order is never changed after the first paint: no fallback ordering and re-sort.
items.acceptance:
- Returning Today → progress has 0 long tasks and is ≤ 80% of the lane base's median (runtime lens: 107 → 79).
- intl-tables.test: the tables equal Intl.DateTimeFormat narrow weekday output for 'he' and 'en', and groupDigits equals toLocaleString('en-US') for 0…10^7 samples.
- perf-runtime e2e: vocab and expressions order and labels are identical to the base on the first frame.
- Returning Today → expressions ≥ 15 ms faster at 4x.
items.risk: The ICU output must stay identical, which the test guards. If the idle warm-up has not run before a very quick first tap, that open pays the old first-use cost: no regression.

items.title: periodReport: ISO string compare and a single sort
items.problem: inP and inPrev build two Dates per attempt and per event. topicMastery runs twice with separate sorts. A heavy Today → progress has a 127-175 ms long task.
items.fix: Convert since and prevSince to ISO strings once and compare a.at as strings, with the dayOf canonical-ISO guard. Build `before` from the already-sorted list in one pass.
items.acceptance:
- Heavy Today → progress ≤ 130 ms at 4x (base 194-224), longest task ≤ 80 ms.
- model-equivalence.test: periodReport output deep-equals the old output for 7, 30 and 90-day periods on both seeds.
items.risk: The report numbers must stay identical; the test guards this.

items.title: Vocab list: one RelativeTimeFormat and one Collator per render, not per row and per comparison
items.problem: A heavy Today → vocab takes 169 ms (light: 51). vocab.js:102 calls relativeDue() for every row, and relativeDue (:31) builds a new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat each time. vocab.js:74 sorts with a.localeCompare(b, 'en', {sensitivity:'base'}), which builds a collator per comparison. Node micro-benchmark for 700 words: 35.4 ms vs 0.4 ms for the formatter and 29.4 ms vs 0.4 ms for the sort, unthrottled (about 4x on the phone). slang.js:45 has the same sort pattern (60 entries).
items.fix: relativeDue takes the formatter from util.relTime(lang) (R6). It keeps its exported signature, plus an optional third parameter for tests. Sort with util.collatorEn().compare. Same in slang.js byTerm.
items.acceptance:
- Heavy Today → vocab ≤ 100 ms at 4x (base 169), longest task ≤ 60 ms.
- Unit test: relativeDue output equals the old implementation for 1,000 random offsets in 'he' and 'en'; the sorted vocab order equals the old order on the heavy seed.
- The axe e2e shows 0 new violations.
items.risk: None: same Intl options, so identical output. The memo is keyed by language, so a UI language switch gets the right formatter.

lanes.title: Generated content index, split and pool files, and their consumers
owns: tests/e2e/*.mjs that exist today, except tests/e2e/run.mjs

items.title: Generator for index, per-item and per-level pool files, plus the content.js API, with a drift test
items.problem: Today, the hubs and the lesson end read only list fields, yet download real-life/scenarios.json (131 KB gz), writing/exercises.json (54 KB) and writing/assignments.json (29 KB). A scenario or an essay needs one item. Drills and level checks need only the auto-graded exercises of a few levels, yet load all 75 lesson files (753 KB gz).
items.fix:
tools/build-content-index.mjs is deterministic, uses sorted keys, and is run by hand like build-manifest. It writes:
- content/real-life/index.json: {id, module, level, title_en, title_he, goal, n_practice}.
- content/real-life/scenario/<id>.json.
- content/writing/index.json, with {exercises, assignments} rows {id, stage, level, kind, title_en, title_he, word_range, min_words, max_words, time_limit_min, n_items, prompt}. These are the field names today.js:522 and adaptive.js:305-309 read; see R9 for n_items.
- content/writing/task/<id>.json.
- content/centers/{read,listen,speak}.json: {lessons:{id:{id, level, title_en, title_he, topics}}, items:[{lesson, ex}]} in curriculum rank order.
- content/pool/<level>.json: [{lesson, level, topics, pitfalls, ex}] for pool.AUTO_TYPES exercises, in lesson order. Computed sizes: PreA1 28, A1 51, A2 56, B1 55, B2 39, C1 38 and C2 30 KB gz.
content.js adds scenarioIndex(), scenario(id), writingIndex(), writingTask(id), center(name) and pool(level), all memoised. The old methods stay for tools and tests. validate-content and content-index.test check that every index row and split file equals its source fields.
items.acceptance:
- content-index.test passes and fails on a hand-edited source.
- Two generator runs are byte-identical.
- real-life index ≤ 8 KB gz (prototype 6.1); largest scenario file ≤ 6 KB gz; writing index ≤ 3 KB gz (prototype 2.1); largest pool file ≤ 60 KB gz.
- npm run validate passes.
items.risk: Two sources of truth, so the generated files and the drift test are mandatory. Ids used as file names must be URL-safe: encodeURIComponent, and the test rejects '/'.

items.title: Today and the lesson end read the index
items.problem: Cold Today waits on scenarios.json, which ends at 3361 of 3695 ms. lesson.js:500 downloads 185 KB gz in the background of every cold lesson.
items.fix: today.js:228 and lesson.js:500 use scenarioIndex() and writingIndex(). Assignments come from the writing index (its assignments rows). learner.todayPlan, pickScenario, pickWritingTask and writingMinutes receive index rows. They work on them unchanged once R9 is merged (contract C-11), so C2 merges after R9. The Today view also starts the next lesson's fetch alongside the lists, as in the prototype.
items.acceptance:
- Standalone: cold Today ≤ 2600 ms (3695; re-measured prototype 2462) and ≤ 240 KB gz (prototype 226); cold lesson ≤ 340 KB gz on the wire (507).
- Integrated: cold Today ≤ 1950 ms and ≤ 180 KB gz.
- e2e first-run-today and r4-today-path pass.
- The Today plan, including each block's minutes, is identical for 5 seeded learners (unit snapshot), among them one whose writing pick is a sentence-exercise task.

items.title: Real-life hub, scenario, simulations, practice, onboarding and profile on the index
items.problem: reallife.js:107, simulations.js:15, practice.js:26, onboarding.js:81 and profile.js:46 download the full 542 KB file for list fields. scenario.js:34 needs one scenario.
items.fix: The list views use scenarioIndex() and read n_practice instead of practice.length. scenario.js loads scenario(id), and builds its 'next scenario' list from the index after the first render. After this item, grep finds no js/ caller of content.scenarios(), writingExercises() or assignments() outside content.js, apart from the feature-detected fallback in the router (C-1).
items.acceptance:
- Cold real-life ≤ 600 ms faster than the lane base (measured −639), and cold scenario likewise (measured −644).
- Integrated: real-life ≤ 1850 ms, scenario ≤ 1900 ms.
- The real-life e2e suites pass.
- A scenario opens offline after the precache install (delivery's offline sweep).

items.title: Reading, listening and speaking list from centre files, not 74 lessons, with an offline fallback
items.problem: center.js:18 gatherExercises → allLessons. Cold reading is 7172 ms, 106 requests, 1059 KB gz. First-session Today → reading is 4157 ms of spinner.
items.fix:
gatherExercises(types) loads center(name) for the requested types and keeps the rank order lesson*100 + index. Items keep their lesson id, because exercise ids are unique only per lesson. The centre views read only lesson id, level, title_en, title_he and topics (audited), which the centre file carries. findItem works on the same items.
If center(name) rejects (offline, and the file was never cached), it falls back to the current allLessons path. Offline that returns only the lessons cached on the device, so the screen still lists them, as today.
items.acceptance:
- Standalone: cold reading ≤ 3100 ms with ≤ 35 requests and ≤ 380 KB gz; listening ≤ 3000 ms (7255).
- First-session Today → reading ≤ 300 ms (4157); returning ≤ 100 ms (382).
- center.test: the item list and order equal the allLessons path for read, listen+dictation and speak.
- The practice-hubs e2e passes.
- Offline e2e: with 2 lessons saved and Reading never opened online, #/reading lists their reading texts, as on the base.
items.risk: The screens now list texts whose lesson file is not cached. They still open from the centre file, so this is better offline, but the e2e assertions on the lists must be reviewed. The centre files are not precached: they are cached on first use (contract C-2).

items.title: Drills and level checks from per-level pool files, not 75 lessons
items.problem: pool.js:65 exercisePool() → content.allLessons() serves drillSet (drill.js, the plan's practice block) and checkpointSet (checkpoint.js). Re-measured on the base: cold #/checkpoint/A1 7320 ms, 107 requests, 1065 KB gz; first-session Today → checkpoint 6286 ms; returning 391 ms. checkpointSet uses only one level; drillSet uses only levels ≤ level+1.
items.fix:
exercisePool(levels) loads content.pool(l) for the requested levels and builds the same items ({ex, lesson, level, topic, topics, pitfalls, errors}), memoised per level.
- checkpointSet(level) requests [level].
- drillSet requests the levels up to maxLevel (its eligible filter). With no level, it requests all levels.
- If pool(l) rejects (offline and never cached), it falls back to the current allLessons path for that level, which offline returns only the lessons cached on the device, as today.
drill.js and checkpoint.js keep their calls unchanged.
items.acceptance:
- Standalone: cold checkpoint/A1 ≤ 3300 ms with ≤ 30 requests and ≤ 300 KB gz (7320 / 107 / 1065).
- First-session Today → checkpoint/A1 ≤ 700 ms (6286); returning ≤ 150 ms (391).
- pool.test:
  - For each level, the pool items equal the allLessons-derived items (deep-equal, errors as sorted arrays).
  - With a seeded Math.random, checkpointSet and drillSet return the same sets before and after.
- Offline e2e: with A1 lessons saved, #/checkpoint/A1 behaves as on the base.
items.risk: Item order inside the pool must match the old lesson order, or seeded sets differ; the test guards it. Pool files are cached on first use, not precached (contract C-2).

items.title: Writing hub and essay on the writing index; final-* assignments fetched lazily
items.problem: After Today stops warming exercises.json and assignments.json, the first-session Today → writing regressed to 1112 ms in the combined prototype. essay.js:111 downloads both full files for one task.
items.fix: writing.js lists from writingIndex() and reads n_items. essay.js loads writingTask(id) plus the index. Assignment files for final-* tasks are fetched only when packOf() is first needed, after the first render.
items.acceptance:
- Integrated: cold writing ≤ 2050 ms; cold final-B2 ≤ 2600 ms.
- First-session Today → writing ≤ 350 ms; Today → final-B2 ≤ 150 ms (95).
- Essay typing targets hold (per-key p95 ≤ 22 ms).
- The writing e2e suites pass.
items.risk: packOf timing changes; a test must cover a final task's pack opening offline and online.

items.title: Index attempts by lesson and exercise in center.js
items.problem: attemptsOn (center.js:31) filters every attempt for each row, for doneCount, per level group and in nextSuggestion: O(items × attempts). A heavy reading open has 2 long tasks, the longest 125-152 ms.
items.fix: Build a WeakMap keyed on the attempts array that maps `${lesson}\0${exercise}` to a list, once per array. attemptsOn becomes a lookup. Callers must not mutate the result; none do.
items.acceptance:
- With --learner heavy at 4x: Today → reading TBT ≤ 10 ms (94), longest task ≤ 60 ms.
- center.test: identical done counts and suggestions.
items.risk: Shared arrays could be mutated by a future caller; freeze them in tests. The cache is keyed on the array identity, so a new attempts array (after a recordAttempt) rebuilds it.

items.title: Today draws once; day checks via util.dayOf in today.js and lesson.js
items.problem: Today runs draw() twice per load: once inside the initial loadLesson (today.js:248), once as the main draw. today.js:284 and lesson.js:463, 469 and 636 build a Date per record.
items.fix: The initial loadLesson only sets extras.lesson, so the single main draw follows. Later loadLesson and loadPaces calls still redraw. The day checks use util.dayOf, feature-detected per contract C-3 (fallback: todayKey(new Date(x))).
items.acceptance:
- A performance.mark('today:draw') count of 1 per Today load for a day-1 learner (e2e probe).
- Heavy warm Today ≤ 750 ms at 4x once R2-R4 are merged.
- Light Today shows no regression beyond +15 ms.
items.risk: A missing redraw when the lesson arrives late; e2e r4-today-path must still show the lesson card.

items.title: Digit grouping in writing.js and essay.js without Intl
items.problem: writing.js:16 and essay.js:564 call toLocaleString('en-US'), which costs 35-39 ms on first use. It is the long task on Today → writing.
items.fix: Use util.groupDigits per contract C-3, falling back to the current call if it is absent.
items.acceptance:
- Returning Today → writing ≤ 75 ms with 0 long tasks (lens base 90).
- The essay word-count labels are identical (the R6 test plus an e2e text check).
items.risk: Integers only; word counts are integers.

items.title: List-only reading index; the passage is loaded when a text is opened
items.problem: After C4, reading still downloads 92 KB gz of passages (centers/read.json in the prototype) just to list about 73 rows.
items.fix: Make content/centers/read.json list-only: lesson, exercise id, title or first words, word count, question count. On open, findItem → content.lesson(l) supplies the passage. Keep this item only if the gate in the acceptance holds.
items.risk: Opening a passage costs one lesson fetch, and reading offline depends on cached lessons. That is why it is gated.

lanes.title: Critical path, route prefetch, release handoff, perceived load and shell stability
owns: css/app.css (boot frame, .booting and shell rules, in one marked block)

items.title: Preload the late boot modules and the two boot JSON files
items.problem:
Two requests start late in the boot:
- session.js and placement.js are in app.js's static import closure but missing from index.html's modulepreload list (confirmed by an import scan). They start at 1062 and 1182 ms, in a second module wave.
- curriculum.json (16.6 KB gz) and manifest.json start at about 1557 ms, after module evaluation and the IndexedDB open.
items.fix:
In index.html, add:
- <link rel=modulepreload> for js/core/session.js and js/core/placement.js;
- <link rel=preload as=fetch crossorigin> for content/curriculum.json and content/manifest.json. crossorigin makes the request mode match content.js's plain fetch().
boot-preload.test checks that the modulepreload list equals app.js's static import closure, and that both preloaded JSON files are fetched at boot.
items.acceptance:
- Cold welcome and cold Today each ≥ 120 ms faster than the lane base (measured −164 and −161).
- curriculum.json requestStart ≤ 650 ms on cold Today.
- Every preloaded URL is requested exactly once (Resource Timing: 0 duplicates).
- boot-preload.test passes, and fails when an import is added without a preload.
items.risk: Very low. Without crossorigin the JSON would download twice; the duplicate check catches that. manifest.json must stay small, which is why D1 puts the hashes in release.json.

items.title: Preload each route's whole module graph from a generated map
items.problem: Lazy views discover their imports one level at a time. A cold lesson has 4 request levels at 150 ms RTT (lesson.js → exercise/player → grading → writing-analyzer).
items.fix: tools/build-route-deps.mjs writes js/core/route-deps.js from a static import scan: {route pattern: [modules beyond the boot list]}. router.go() calls preloadRoute(match) before match.load(), which appends modulepreload links once per module. After Today renders, it preloads the lesson route at idle. router.test fails if route-deps.js is stale. No bundling.
items.acceptance:
- Each of cold lesson, cold games and cold final-B2 is ≥ 250 ms faster than the lane base (measured −270, −346 and −398).
- First-session Today → lesson ≥ 40% faster (measured 1329 → 685).
- Cold welcome and Today regress by no more than 30 ms.
- The stale-map test passes.
items.risk: A stale map costs only speed, never correctness, because import() still resolves. A preload for a route the learner leaves at once wastes a little bandwidth.

items.title: The router starts each route's content fetch as the route resolves; Today prefetches the next lesson
items.risk: The map can drift from what the views read; a drifted entry only loses the gain. A failed prefetch must not cache a rejected promise; content.js already deletes failed entries.

items.title: Page side of the service-worker update handoff: switch release at the next path change, in every tab
items.problem:
With cache-first code (D2), a new release would otherwise reach the learner only after every tab closes. Activating in the middle of a session could mix old in-memory modules with new lazy ones. The only lazy imports are the router's view imports; speech.js imports components.js, which is already in the boot graph.
An SPA rarely navigates, so the browser's update check (on navigation) seldom runs for a learner who resumes the app from the background.
items.fix:
In app.js and router.js:
- Watch registration.waiting and updatefound. On visibilitychange to visible, call registration.update() if the last check is over 1 hour old.
- In router.go, after the old view's cleanup and store.flush(), and before match.load():
  - if a new worker is waiting, post {type:'lucid:activate'} to it (contract C-4), wait for controllerchange (at most 3 s), then location.replace the target hash. If it times out, continue normally.
  - if this tab already saw a controllerchange it did not request, reload to the target hash without posting.
  - this applies only when the path changes; a query-only change (keepScroll, centre ?l=&e=) never reloads.
- On visibilitychange to hidden, do the same only when the current route is not bare and has no query.
- Do nothing on the first install.
items.acceptance:
- Scenario u: the new release's code runs no later than the first path change after its install completes; the probe reads RELEASE.
- perf-boot e2e:
  - no reload during an in-progress lesson or essay;
  - the essay draft and the lesson's resume point survive a reload triggered by leaving them;
  - with two tabs, the second tab reloads at its next path change and never imports a module from the other release.
- 0 page loads mix modules from two releases (the harness checks each module's cache via SW-tagged responses).
- At most 1 reload per release per tab.
items.risk: An unexpected reload costs about 0.4 s warm, once per release, at a moment the learner is changing screen anyway. If the old view's cleanup throws, the router already logs it and continues; the store is flushed before the reload.

items.title: Desktop CLS: hide the main column until the shell is drawn
items.problem: On desktop, div.main jumps from 248 to 1192 px wide when drawShell shows the rail. CLS is 0.186-0.500 on every load, warm loads included.
items.fix:
- index.html: <html class=booting>; the first spinner gets the classes boot and boot-first.
- app.css: `.booting .main {visibility:hidden}`, and a fixed `.boot-first` with visibility:visible, so the spinner (role=status) stays visible and announced.
- drawShell, and the boot error path, remove the 'booting' class first.
items.acceptance:
- Desktop CLS ≤ 0.01 on all scenario b and c loads (base 0.186-0.500).
- Mobile CLS 0.
- Desktop view times within +15 ms.
- perf-boot e2e: a forced boot error still shows its message.
- axe: 0 new violations.
items.risk: If boot throws before drawShell, the content stays hidden, so the error path must remove the class (tested). The skip-link target is hidden for a few frames.

items.title: Branded boot frame that paints before the stylesheet arrives
items.problem: On a cold phone visit the screen is blank (white in dark mode) until 1.55 s, then shows only a spinner until the view.
items.fix:
As prototype proto3b:
- index.html: an inline <style> with the light and dark ground colours, plus a .bootframe holding the 'Lucid' wordmark and a spinner, aria-hidden. The CSP already allows inline styles.
- <link rel=preload as=style href=css/app.css> in the head.
- The module script moves from the end of <body>, where it is today, into the head. If it stayed after the in-body stylesheet, it would wait for it (proto3: views 110-150 ms slower, CLS 0.082).
- The stylesheet <link> moves to the start of <body>, right after the frame.
- app.css hides .bootframe once the shell or a bare route is drawn.
- A unit test keeps the frame colours equal to the app.css tokens.
items.acceptance:
- Mobile cold first paint and FCP ≤ 700 ms on welcome and Today (base 1552/2072 and 1560/1868; proto3b 624/620).
- Views regress by no more than 30 ms.
- CLS 0 on mobile and desktop.
- The axe e2e shows 0 new violations.
- Dark mode never paints white (a screenshot pixel check on the first frame).
items.risk: It relies on a stylesheet in the body blocking rendering (Chrome) and on :has(). In older browsers the opaque frame covers the shell until the CSS loads. FCP now measures a placeholder, so report the view separately. If D9 inlines the CSS, the frame stays harmless.

items.title: fitTitle after render, with a cached size probe
items.problem: drawShell runs fitTitle synchronously while the old view is still in the DOM. That forces layout (5.5-11.8 ms per transition), and the 18-probe sectionTitleSize runs once per page load (about 27 ms at 4x).
items.fix: Run fitTitle in requestAnimationFrame after the view renders. Cache titleFit in localStorage, inside try/catch, keyed by `${lang}|${base}|${width}|${CSS_VERSION}`.
items.acceptance:
- Page-load script time ≥ 15 ms lower at 4x (trace).
- Returning-transition long tasks are not worse.
- Mobile and desktop CLS stay ≤ 0.01.
- shell-r4.test passes.
items.risk: One frame at the default size: the box size is fixed, so CLS should stay 0, and the check above verifies it. A stale cache after a CSS change is avoided by the version key.

items.title: Drop the rubik-latin font preload (keep Hebrew)
items.problem: The 35 KB Latin font competes with the CSS and modules in wave 1, for a UI that paints Hebrew first (rubik-hebrew is 9 KB).
items.fix: Remove the rubik-latin preload link from index.html. Keep rubik-hebrew. The font loads on demand through @font-face (font-display: swap).
items.acceptance:
- Keep only if cold welcome is ≥ 50 ms faster (measured −82), and both mobile and desktop CLS stay ≤ 0.01 on all loads.
- Revert otherwise.
items.risk: A fallback-font swap for English text. CLS was measured as 0 on the phone, but desktop must be re-checked after B4.

lanes.title: Service worker, release hashing, deploy-time minify and verification

items.title: Per-file content hashes in release.json and an automatic RELEASE that also covers sw.js
items.problem: RELEASE is bumped by hand (sw.js:8). Cache-first code is safe only if every deploy that changes a byte, sw.js included, changes the release, and the incremental install needs a per-file hash. A release hash over the precached files alone would stay the same when only sw.js changes (scenario u), so the new worker would reuse the live cache name.
items.fix:
build-manifest.mjs exports buildManifest(root) and writes release.json at the app root:
- hashes: {path: sha256 prefix} for every precached file, including SHELL, and for every content/lessons/*.json;
- release: a hash of all those hashes plus sw.js with its RELEASE line normalised.
It rewrites the RELEASE line in sw.js to that value. release.json is in SHELL. content/manifest.json keeps its current fields only, because it is on the boot path (B1). offline-manifest.test recomputes both and fails when they are stale.
items.acceptance:
- offline-manifest.test fails after any 1-byte edit to a precached file, a lesson file or the logic of sw.js, until build-manifest is re-run, then passes.
- 100% of hashes match the served bytes (verify.mjs).
- sw.js RELEASE equals release.json release.
- manifest.json stays ≤ 1 KB gz.
items.risk: A developer forgetting to run the tool; the failing test blocks that. Every lane that edits a precached file must re-run the tool; the merge rule is contract C-12.

items.title: Code served cache-first from the release cache
items.problem: Network-first code (sw.js:50-58) waits on 30 revalidations after 10 minutes (1269-1284 ms) and re-downloads 428 KB after any push to main (2099-2111 ms). On lie-fi it waits 4 s per request in sequence (16.5 s).
items.fix:
isCode requests are answered with cache.match(req), with './' for navigations, and go to the network only on a miss, storing the response. Freshness comes from the release: the browser re-checks sw.js on navigation, bypassing the HTTP cache (the default updateViaCache 'imports'), and B6 adds a check on resume.
Update docs/architecture.md §7, and re-review security finding S-15 in fix-log.md and security-review.md: a fix now arrives through D1 and B6 at the first path change after install. Get a security sign-off.
items.risk: Learners keep stale code if RELEASE does not change, which D1 prevents. It reverses S-15, so it needs sign-off.

items.title: Controlled activation in the worker, plus the legacy upgrade path
items.problem: The current skipWaiting (sw.js:33) and clients.claim (:39) activate a new release in the middle of a session. With cache-first code, that would serve new lazy modules to an old page.
items.fix:
sw.js calls skipWaiting only in two cases:
- when there is no active worker (first install, which keeps clients.claim so the first page becomes controlled);
- on message {type:'lucid:activate'} from a client (contract C-4).
One-time path: when the only existing Lucid caches use the legacy hand-bumped RELEASE format, it also activates immediately with claim, as today, so learners on the old app.js are not stranded.
items.risk: A waiting worker never activates if no page sends the message. Browsers still activate it when all clients close. The legacy path keeps today's behaviour for one release only.

items.title: Lean precache that revalidates, code before content
items.problem: The install uses cache:'reload' and so re-downloads what the page just fetched (884 KB). It also holds files no view needs once the indexes exist, and competes with the first session (first-session Today → lesson 1911 ms). The unmodified index prototype grew the precache to 152 requests and 1094 KB, because it listed the centre files.
items.fix:
- Fetch with new Request(u, {cache:'no-cache'}): a 304 reuses the HTTP-cached body.
- Code (js/, vendor, config) first, content second.
- The offline list (contract C-2) includes the index and split files, route-deps.js and release.json. It excludes content/centers/ and content/pool/, and excludes scenarios.json, exercises.json and assignments.json when their index exists.
- Drop fonts/rubik-latin-ext.woff2 from SHELL (unicode-range loads it on demand).
- Do not store './' and 'index.html' twice: one entry, and match the other to it.
- No concurrency limit.
- tests/e2e/run.mjs gains an offline sweep: after install, with the network cut, every route in the 13-route list renders.
items.acceptance:
- Scenario f: welcome precache ≤ 700 KB on the wire (884) and ≤ 160 requests, finished ≤ 8.5 s (9.45 s).
- First-session Today → lesson ≥ 25% faster than the lane base.
- Offline sweep 13/13.
- sw.test passes, including the no-cache request mode.
items.risk: cache:'no-cache' always revalidates with the server, so the browser HTTP cache cannot supply an outdated copy. The remaining risk is a CDN edge still serving the previous deploy's file right after a push; D5's hash check detects it. Offline, accented Latin letters use the fallback font until rubik-latin-ext has been fetched once.

items.title: Incremental install: copy unchanged files and carry saved lessons over
items.problem: Every release downloads all 884 KB again, takes 11 s, and deletes the learner's saved offline lessons (4 → 0). Next-open Today then takes 1115 ms.
items.risk: Wrong hashes would copy stale files forward, which D1's test and the hash check on fetch prevent. The install code grows in complexity, so it is covered by tests.

items.title: Non-lesson content, fonts and vendor served from the release cache
items.problem: After a push to main, stale-while-revalidate re-downloads about 300 KB of unchanged content, fonts and vendor files in the background of every open: GitHub Pages ETags change on every deploy (re-measured: 299 KB with cache-first code).
items.fix: Route content/ (except content/lessons/, content/centers/ and content/pool/), fonts/ and vendor/ cache-first from the release cache. Lessons, centre and pool files stay stale-while-revalidate. D5 refreshes only the files whose hash changed.
items.acceptance:
- Scenario g after a push: ≤ 15 KB downloaded while opening Today (base 298 KB after D2, 428 before), and ≤ 1 content request.
- sw.test routing cases pass.
items.risk: A content fix reaches learners only through a new release hash, which D1 guarantees whenever build-manifest is run (enforced by the test).

items.title: Deploy-only minify step in pages.yml (paths kept, source maps, fail-safe), gated on measured gain
items.problem: JS is 438 KB gz and CSS 37 KB gz unminified (32 KB of the CSS is comments). Minification measured −349 ms on cold welcome and −374 ms on cold Today.
items.fix:
tools/build/package.json and its lockfile pin esbuild 0.25.10 exactly. build.mjs:
- minifies in place js/**, vendor/*.mjs, config.js and css/app.css (format esm, target esnext, legalComments inline, external .map files with a sourceMappingURL comment; CSS with supported:{'color-functions':true}, so oklch is not rounded);
- compacts content/**/*.json;
- re-runs buildManifest on the built bytes and re-stamps RELEASE.
verify.mjs checks that every module parses, every import resolves, every .map exists and every hash matches.
In pages.yml, add one step before the 'Exclude…' rm: `cd lucid && (npm ci --prefix tools/build && node tools/build/build.mjs && node tools/build/verify.mjs) || (git checkout -- . && git clean -fdq -- .)`, so any failure deploys the unminified source without stray build files, and the other sites are untouched.
Amend ADR-1: the source stays buildless; the deploy-only transform is auditable through the maps.
items.acceptance:
- Keep only if, on the integrated tree, both cold welcome and cold Today are ≥ 200 ms faster than the unminified build of the same commit.
- Total JS ≤ 330 KB gz; CSS ≤ 23 KB gz.
- E2E_ROOT=<built> full e2e: the same pass count as on the source.
- Pixel diff of 13 routes at 390 px: 0 differing pixels.
- Build ≤ 10 s; a forced error falls back to the source tree with no .map files left (tested locally).
items.risk: A behaviour change from minification is unlikely: no eval, new Function or Function.name in js/. Stack traces need the maps, which are published; the source is public anyway. Dropped if the gate fails.

items.title: Non-gating CI check of the built site
items.problem: The built tree must stay correct after every push. Making the deploy job depend on an e2e run would block the other sites in pages.yml.
items.acceptance:
- A workflow_dispatch run on the lane branch is green.
- Its e2e pass count equals the local source run.
- A deliberately broken import on a scratch branch turns it red.
items.risk: CI minutes only; no effect on deploys.

items.title: Inline the minified CSS at deploy time, gated
items.problem: After minification the stylesheet (22 KB gz) is still a render-blocking request on cold loads.
items.fix: build.mjs replaces exactly the <link rel=stylesheet href=css/app.css> in index.html, wherever B5 put it, with a <style> of the minified CSS, rewriting url(../fonts/ to url(fonts/. The transform fails safe if the tag is not found. css/app.css stays deployed, because privacy.html links it.
items.risk: A future removal of 'unsafe-inline' from style-src would also mean undoing this. Gated, so dropped if warm regresses.

rejected.title: Per-route bundling with esbuild code splitting
rejected.reason: Measured (b1): lesson −149 ms but welcome +121 and Today +143. Wrapper chunks add a request level. A preloaded route graph (B2) gains more and keeps one file per module (ADR-1).

rejected.title: Splitting the CSS per route, or extracting critical CSS
rejected.reason: After minification, per-route splitting saves at most 10-15 KB gz, about 75 ms (estimated). Critical CSS (31% of rules used) would need every state covered and risks unstyled flashes; D9 inlining is simpler.

rejected.title: Streaming JSON, or parsing JSON in a worker
rejected.reason: Measured: JSON.parse of the largest file (477 KB) takes 5.6 ms at 4x; Response.json() takes at most 27 ms. Bytes and fetch timing are the bottleneck, and those are addressed.

rejected.title: Store compaction into snapshot rows (opt3)
rejected.reason: −118 ms only for heavy learners. It changes the on-disk format (sync, export and import, eraseDevice) and adds a 170-209 ms compaction long task. Deferred: revisit if heavy warm Today is still over 750 ms after R2-R4.

rejected.title: Archiving or summarising old attempts
rejected.reason: Changes the learner model's inputs (mastery time-weighting, evidence windows) and the synced attempts collection. Needs product and sync design; not measured.

rejected.title: Limiting precache concurrency (s2 / proto2c)
rejected.reason: Measured no gain: lesson 1417 vs 1434 ms and 1318 vs 1314 ms.

rejected.title: Caching Intl objects at module level to remove the first-use cost
rejected.reason: Measured no change for the first use: creating the first object (ICU data load) is the cost. R6 removes or pre-warms that use instead. This does not apply to repeated construction: vocab.js builds a formatter per row and a collator per comparison, which R8 fixes.

rejected.title: Lazy-loading sync.js, session.js and api.js when accounts are not configured
rejected.reason: Estimated 10-15 ms of compile. It risks the email-link login handled at start-up and delays sync for signed-in users. B1 instead preloads session.js as part of the static graph.

rejected.title: Keeping the module script at the end of <body>, after an in-body stylesheet (proto3)
rejected.reason: Measured: views 110-150 ms slower and CLS 0.082, because the script then waits for the stylesheet. B5 moves the script into the head (proto3b), which kept the views at baseline.

rejected.title: Loading the route module from app.js right after openStore (p3)
rejected.reason: Measured no gain (3092 vs 3130 ms, noise): the gap is evaluation and IndexedDB work, not network. B2 and B3 address the real waterfall.

rejected.title: Removing all font preloads (f1)
rejected.reason: Within noise on Today, and the Hebrew UI must paint in its font first. Only the Latin preload removal is kept, as gated B8.

rejected.title: Navigation preload
rejected.reason: With HTML served cache-first from the release cache (D2), there is no network-first navigation left to speed up.

rejected.title: Precaching the centre files (read, listen, speak) and the pool files
rejected.reason: Measured +210 KB gz and an install 2.5 s longer for the centre files, competing with the first session; the pool files would add about 300 KB gz more. They are cached on first use instead. C4 and C10 fall back to the lessons cached on the device when offline, as today.

rejected.title: Partial rendering of the vocab list ('show more')
rejected.reason: Breaks find-in-page and screen-reader access to the full list. R8 removes the per-row Intl cost with every row in the DOM.

rejected.title: content-visibility: auto on vocab rows (the previous R8)
rejected.reason: The measured heavy-vocab cost is mostly per-row RelativeTimeFormat construction and a per-comparison collator, which R8 removes. The rows expand in place (aria-expanded), so a wrong intrinsic size makes the scroll jump. Revisit only if heavy Today → vocab is still over 120 ms after R8. This also leaves css/app.css to a single lane.

rejected.title: Rendering vocab and expressions with a toLowerCase order and re-sorting after idle
rejected.reason: Reordering a list after it is painted shifts rows on screen (CLS) and moves items under a screen reader's cursor. Shared module-level Intl objects plus an idle warm-up (R6, R8) give the final order on the first frame.

rejected.title: Starting the content precache only when the page reports idle
rejected.reason: Not measured. It lengthens the window in which a first-time visitor who goes offline lacks content. D4 (revalidating, lean, code first) addresses the contention with measured gains.

rejected.title: Per-level pool files for the word game (wordgame.js lesson loading)
rejected.reason: The measured cold games route does not fetch all lessons (34 requests, 252 KB gz). Drills and level checks, which do, are now C10.

rejected.title: updateViaCache: 'none' on the service-worker registration
rejected.reason: The security review already showed it changes nothing: the default 'imports' bypasses the HTTP cache for sw.js, which imports nothing.

rejected.title: Today skeleton in place of the spinner
rejected.reason: Not prototyped. B5's boot frame plus a cold Today about 1.7 s faster cover most of the perceived gap, at lower a11y risk.

rejected.title: A deploy job gated on the e2e suite inside pages.yml
rejected.reason: A Lucid test failure would block the unrelated sites in the same deploy job. Verification runs in a separate non-gating workflow (D8), and the build step falls back to the source tree on failure (D7).

contracts:
C-1 content.js API (content lane):
- content.scenarioIndex(), content.scenario(id), content.writingIndex(), content.writingTask(id), content.center('read'|'listen'|'speak') and content.pool(level) return memoised promises; scenario(id) and writingTask(id) resolve to null on a 404.
- The old content.scenarios(), writingExercises(), assignments() and allLessons() stay working.
- Consumers in other lanes (the boot router's DATA map) call the new methods feature-detected, e.g. `content.scenario?.(id) ?? content.scenarios()` and `content.pool?.(level)`, so either merge order works.

C-2 Generated content paths (content lane writes, delivery lane lists):
- content/real-life/index.json, content/real-life/scenario/<id>.json, content/writing/index.json, content/writing/task/<id>.json, content/centers/{read,listen,speak}.json and content/pool/<level>.json.
- build-manifest's offline list includes the index and split files. It excludes content/centers/ and content/pool/, which are cached on first use, and excludes real-life/scenarios.json, writing/exercises.json and writing/assignments.json whenever the corresponding index file exists (existsSync).
- Views that read centre or pool files fall back to the cached-lessons path when the file cannot be loaded.
- The source files stay in the repository for the tools.

C-3 util.js exports (runtime lane):
- dayOf(iso): canonical '…Z' strings are sliced; other values fall back to todayKey(new Date(x)).
- groupDigits(n): identical to n.toLocaleString('en-US') for integers.
- collatorEn(), relTime(lang) and warmIntl(): memoised Intl objects, plus an idle warm-up.
- Consumers in other lanes feature-detect:
  - the content lane uses `import * as util from '../core/util.js'` with fallbacks: `(util.dayOf ?? ((x) => util.todayKey(new Date(x))))` and `(util.groupDigits ?? ((n) => n.toLocaleString('en-US')))`;
  - the boot lane calls `util.warmIntl?.()` once in requestIdleCallback after the first route renders.
- Existing exports (todayKey and the others) keep their signatures.

C-4 Service-worker activation protocol (delivery lane: sw.js; boot lane: js/app.js, js/core/router.js):
- The worker calls skipWaiting only when no worker is active, on the one-time upgrade from legacy hand-bumped caches, or on a client message {type:'lucid:activate'}.
- The active worker, at a navigation to the app shell ('' or index.html) while a release waits, posts that message to the waiting worker itself and answers the navigation with a page of its own (never stored, no-store, its inline script and style allowed by a per-response nonce in its own CSP, the app's ground colours and a role=status line) that reloads once the waiting worker is no longer waiting, or after about 2 s. Only navigations within 1 s of the first ask get that page; a later one (also that page's own reload when the browser could not activate the waiting worker because the active one still has a request in hand) is served the app by the active release, so a hand-over that does not happen costs one page.
- A release installs only with its release.json and its whole shell in its cache (a shell write that does not fit the quota fails the install, and the active release stays). Activation deletes older lucid- caches only when its own cache holds release.json and the shell, and never while a newer worker is installing or waiting; an install whose cache was removed while it ran fails.
- The page sends that message only from router.go on a path change, after the old view's cleanup and store.flush(), or when the tab is hidden on a non-bare route without a query. It then replaces the location with the target hash on the resulting controllerchange.
- A tab that sees a controllerchange it did not request reloads at its next path change instead of importing a view module.
- The page calls registration.update() when it becomes visible after more than 1 hour without a check.
- Either side alone degrades to standard behaviour: the worker activates when all tabs close; the page sees no waiting worker.

C-5 Release format (delivery lane):
- content/manifest.json keeps {version, lessons, offline} unchanged and stays small (it is preloaded at boot).
- release.json (app root, precached) holds {release, hashes:{path: sha256-prefix}} for every precached file and every lesson file.
- release = hash(all hashes + sw.js with its RELEASE line normalised); sw.js RELEASE equals release.json release.
- tools/build-manifest.mjs exports buildManifest(root) so the deploy build can recompute both on the built bytes.
- Other lanes never edit these files by hand; they run `node tools/build-manifest.mjs` after rebasing.

C-6 Route map (boot lane): js/core/route-deps.js is generated by tools/build-route-deps.mjs and committed. The deploy build must keep every module path unchanged (no bundling, no renaming), so the map and the modulepreload links stay valid on the built tree. walk('js') puts it in the precache automatically.

C-7 Deploy transform (delivery lane):
- build.mjs edits only files under lucid/ and keeps every path.
- It may replace exactly one tag in index.html, `<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/app.css">`, wherever it sits, and does nothing if it is absent.
- It never touches the CSP meta.
- On any error the pages.yml step restores the source tree with git checkout and git clean inside lucid/, so the other sites deploy unchanged.

C-8 Harness (runtime lane, merged first):
- The existing flags and scenarios a-f keep their meaning and baseline comparability.
- New: --learner light|heavy, --http-maxage N, --etag-epoch, --net offline|lie-fi, scenario g (returning-visit states), scenario u (release update), and the checkpoint/ and drill routes.
- Every lane reports its acceptance as the median of ≥ 3 runs against its own base commit on the same machine, in its own docs/perf/<lane>.md.

C-9 Shared files:
- css/app.css is edited only by the boot lane (boot frame, .booting and shell rules, in one marked block); no lane reformats it.
- js/core/i18n.js is not changed by any lane in this programme.
- New lane e2e files are owned by their lane (tests/e2e/perf-boot.mjs, tests/e2e/perf-runtime.mjs). The existing e2e files except run.mjs belong to the content lane; other lanes run them but do not edit them.

C-10 E2E runner (delivery lane): tests/e2e/run.mjs gains E2E_ROOT (default: the repository) and the offline route sweep. The content lane updates content stubs in the other existing e2e files to the new paths, and keeps stubbing the old paths too until both lanes have merged.

C-11 Index rows in the learner model (runtime lane, merged with R1):
- adaptive.writingMinutes counts `task.n_items ?? task.items?.length`.
- pickScenario, pickWritingTask and todayPlan read only fields that the index rows carry (id, level, stage, module, word_range, min_words, max_words, title_en, title_he).
- The content lane's index rows keep exactly these field names.

C-12 Generated files on merge: content/manifest.json, release.json, the RELEASE line in sw.js, js/core/route-deps.js and all content/** generated files are never hand-merged. On a conflict, the merger takes either side and re-runs build-content-index, build-route-deps and build-manifest, in that order, then runs the drift tests. Only the delivery lane changes sw.js logic and the manifest generator; only the boot lane changes the route-deps generator; only the content lane changes the content generator.
